findings.issue: The batch summary, features list, leaf_matches and research note assert permanent post deletion and restorable post version history, but none of the cited Ghost snapshots documents either capability. The cited README and help pages cover persistent posts, preview, explicit publish/scheduling, publish-date changes, tags, featured posts and route/filter-based collections; no cited Ghost source documents deletion or version restore. This leaves the 'removable' part of the leaf's published-story lifecycle unsupported and overstates the product.
findings.fix: Remove the permanent-deletion and version-history assertions from summary, features, leaf_matches and research service_boundary, or add official Ghost documentation/README that documents deleting published posts and restoring post versions. If no deletion source is available, record the 'removable' lifecycle element as an explicit gap instead of asserting it.

findings.issue: The leaf's curated-presentation core calls for editorially ordered front/section assemblies. The cited Ghost sources describe a reverse-chronological homepage, tag/author collection pages, a featured-status filter and routes.yaml collections selected by tag/filter; they do not show manual editorial ordering or re-ranking of a front or section page. The batch/leaf_match phrase 'featured posts, tag archives and custom-routed curated collections' therefore overstates the evidence.
findings.fix: Add a source showing manual editorial ordering/re-ranking of a Ghost front or section page, or narrow the leaf match to tag/featured/route-based groupings and state that ordering is automated/chronological. Do not present filter-based collections as equivalent to editorially ordered assemblies.

findings.issue: The batch presents persistent Planning Items/Events, coverage assignment, planning/due dates and assignment views as the system's core, but the official overview lists Planning as an optional module ('Superdesk core and its optional modules ... may use some, all, or none'), and the same overview says Superdesk publishes to websites, apps and partners. The entry does not disclose that the leaf's assignment/schedule core depends on an optional module, and its statement that public publication remains the adjacent leaf is too absolute.
findings.fix: State that Planning (and Broadcasting) are optional modules and scope the leaf match to a Superdesk deployment with Planning enabled; acknowledge Superdesk's end-to-end publishing capability instead of saying public publication is adjacent, or add core documentation showing planning/assignment without the optional module.

non_blocking_notes.note: The Rightsline homepage body supports a central IP-asset repository and rights/availability calculations; 'Avails and Conflict Engine' appears only as a navigation label, so it should not be treated as core workflow proof. The commercial basic type match is still supported by the body text.

Only a homepage was captured; no grant structure, conflict-check workflow, expiry/renewal or territory/window detail is documented. This is acceptable for a commercial basic match but limits the depth of the leaf check.

DMP docs state incoming CSV royalty statements are processed into distribution data, but actual outgoing statements must be created in Excel. The batch's 'CSV royalty statement processing' is accurate, yet the final distribution/statement step is external and should be disclosed. The docs also recommend That Green Thing SaaS for multi-publisher/advanced features; the batch lists single-publisher limits but not this related commercial edition.

The Broadcasting detail page is 404 and the only shows/rundowns evidence is a one-line optional-module list; Planning Date is the intended creation date, not a publication slot. The research records the 404, so this is a documented evidence gap rather than an unsupported claim, but adding Broadcasting/rundown docs would strengthen the output-schedule element.

The official overview says Superdesk publishes to websites, apps, partners and other outputs. A product can match both newsroom-management and news-publishing leaves, but the boundary language should acknowledge the overlap.

OJS is primarily a scholarly submission/peer-review system; the entry correctly uses issue publication, versioning and subscriptions as the core and records the absence of advertising/fulfillment evidence. The blocked pkp.sfu.ca homepage fetch is documented and the GitHub/PKP docs are sufficient.

A 404 snapshot for the Broadcasting URL exists under data/collections/sources but is not registered in REVIEW_SOURCES.json. The research fetch_outcomes records the 404, so the gap is documented, but the snapshot inventory is inconsistent.

magazine-periodical-management.service_form: Self-hosted PHP web application; README requires PHP 8.2+ and MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL.
magazine-periodical-management.license: GPL-3.0; the cited LICENSE snapshot decodes to the GNU GPL v3 text, and the README states GNU GPL.
magazine-periodical-management.community_boundary: No separate community/commercial edition found; the GPL-3.0 repository is the product.
magazine-periodical-management.basis: Official README identifies OJS as open-source scholarly journal software. PKP publication docs document Future/Back Issues, issue creation, article scheduling, publish/unpublish/delete and article versioning. Subscriptions docs document subscription types, start/end dates, expiry, renewal reminders and payment records. Content-access docs document open access, subscription and hybrid access at issue/article level. This supports the publication + recurring issue cycle + circulation/subscription core.
magazine-periodical-management.gaps: No advertising or fulfillment machinery; research records this boundary. Peer review is adjacent and not used as core evidence. The pkp.sfu.ca homepage fetch failed, but official GitHub/PKP docs are sufficient.

media-rights-management.service_form: Commercial SaaS/web platform; the homepage links to app.rightsline.com sign-in.
media-rights-management.community_boundary: Commercial product; no open-source/community edition in the sources.
media-rights-management.basis: Official homepage describes a central repository for every IP asset owned, managed, licensed or sellable, rights and availability calculations, IP commerce/royalties, and lists an Avails and Conflict Engine. Basic commercial authenticity and media-rights type match are supported.
media-rights-management.gaps: Only a homepage; no product docs on structured grants, conflict workflow, expiry/renewal or territory/window detail. 'Avails and Conflict Engine' is a nav label, not workflow evidence. Acceptable for commercial basic review, but depth is limited.

music-publishing-management.service_form: Self-hosted Django web application; docs say designed for cloud but installable locally.
music-publishing-management.license: MIT; the LICENSE snapshot is the MIT text and the docs link an MIT License page.
music-publishing-management.community_boundary: MIT open-source app; docs recommend That Green Thing SaaS for advanced/multi-publisher features. The batch discloses single-controlled-publisher limits but not this related commercial edition.
music-publishing-management.basis: Repository metadata and DMP docs describe musical work and recording metadata, writers, work-level manuscript shares, original publishing agreements, share transfer, publisher fees, CWR 2.1-3.1 export/acknowledgement import, and CSV royalty statement processing into distribution data. Works, not recordings, are the ownership unit; the work catalog + entitlement + income-processing core is supported.
music-publishing-management.gaps: Single controlled original publisher and no uncontrolled publisher records; outgoing royalty statements must be created in Excel. These are disclosed in the docs but only partly reflected in the batch. The related That Green Thing SaaS boundary is not mentioned.

news-publishing-platform.service_form: Self-hosted Node.js Ghost or Ghost(Pro) managed hosting; README and deployment sources support both.
news-publishing-platform.license: MIT; README states MIT and the LICENSE snapshot contains the MIT permission text.
news-publishing-platform.community_boundary: MIT open-source core; Ghost(Pro) is managed hosting, not a feature-gated community edition in the sources.
news-publishing-platform.basis: Ghost README/help docs document persistent posts, preview, explicit publish or schedule, publish-date changes, tags, a featured-status filter, tag/author collection pages, and routes.yaml collections selected by tag/filter. The story record + explicit publish gate are supported; curated groupings are partially supported.
news-publishing-platform.gaps: No cited source for permanent post deletion or restorable version history, yet the batch/research claim them; the 'removable' lifecycle element is unverified. Collections are filter/route-based, not demonstrated editorially ordered front/section assemblies. Corrections/unpublish/redirects are not claimed and not evidenced.

newsroom-management-system.service_form: Self-hosted Python backend and Node.js frontend; installation docs support Docker Compose production and local/dev setups.
newsroom-management-system.license: AGPL-3.0; the LICENSE snapshot decodes to the GNU AGPL v3 text.
newsroom-management-system.community_boundary: AGPL-3.0 open source; Planning and Broadcasting are optional modules within the same product, not a separate community edition. The batch calls Broadcasting optional but does not disclose that Planning is optional.
newsroom-management-system.basis: Superdesk overview describes a newsroom system with desks, stages and roles. The Planning doc describes Events and Planning Items, coverage assignment to desks/users, planning date, coverage due dates, assignment views, reassign/priority and desk/stage/role workflow. Installation docs confirm self-hosted deployment. These support the work-item and assignment/task core when Planning is enabled.
newsroom-management-system.gaps: Planning is explicitly optional, yet the batch presents its features as core without disclosure; Broadcasting (shows/rundowns) is optional and only overview-level, with a 404 detail page. Planning Date is the intended creation date, not a publication slot, and no source shows items placed into publication slots or a rundown. The overview also says Superdesk publishes, so the 'publication remains adjacent' boundary is too absolute.

limits: This was a read-only review of input.json, REVIEW_TASK.md, REVIEW_SOURCES.json, batch.json, research.json and the registered snapshots. No app deployment, runtime test, price/architecture research or live web fetch was performed; sha256 values were not recomputed. Several HTML snapshots are single-line and the read tool truncates lines at 2000 characters, so some page text was reviewed through visible fragments and full-file grep rather than complete rendering. Rightsline has only a homepage; the Superdesk Broadcasting detail page is 404; the OJS homepage fetch failed. These limits do not affect the ID/track, license or core-document checks cited, but they do limit depth on marketing/detail pages.
